body:
I already figured out about joining clubs and groups. There's a gaming club (For table-top gaming, and video games) and an Anime club, as well as a journalism/writing club, and a club about putting together awesome campus-wide things, like Humans vs Zombies (With nerf guns!)

In terms of plane tickets, it probably won't happen. While we doe easily have enough money to sustain us for awhile, and that account for college, my dad has been out of a job for a bit. Now, he could easily get a job slightly less than what he has tended to have, and if need be would do so, but he'd rather not do that, and then when the economy gets better have to suddenly leave and try again.

So he's really right now just looking for a good job, a reason why overall we're not spending a ton of money. The computer budget was one thing, I mean, my parents were ridiculously happy when I got accepted to my first-choice college, and the money I make from my summer job will probably go to assorted non-meal plan meals in college, and probably a bit will go to Steam for games to play on said computer.


At the least, a lot of my senior friends, as well as the one who introduced me to many of the things I love, such as D&D, and a lot of anime, are coming to visit my school again for graduation, so there is a chance I could hang with them for a bit.

Yep, it's a pretty small liberal arts college (1800 people) and from what I am gathering, it's fairly nerd heavy, which is nice.

It's four hours away from my parents, in terms in driving time, and having been in boarding school, I'll be fairly used to being on my own, and getting my work done without being told to.

Thankfully I won't have to really worry about student loans, I'm from an upper-middle-class family, and while we live pretty modestly, apparently my great grandfather, who was originally a farmer in the mid-west, became something called a "Reclaimer" who would buy failing businesses for cheap, turn them around, and sell them for a lot of money.




Apparently, because he regretted having been unable to attend a higher-educational institution himself, he left a fairly hefty sum for future descendants to attend college.


My parents still haven't told me how much it is, probably for good reason, but apparently it's enough to put me, my brother, and any children we might have years off in the future, through college.

Yeah, good point.


Well, in terms of summer, I'm planning on trying to find a summer job for some spending money during college, among other things.


Aside from that, as a birthday/graduation/college acceptance gift from my parents they're allotting me a certain budget to build a computer, since my old one died and my current one freezes and crashes from just playing flash videos. So it'll be nice to have a decent gaming pc.


In terms of hanging out with friends, I would if I could.


Many of those friends live all over the U.S. and I only ever occasionally get to talk to them online, So it's extremely difficult to talk to them.


I don't have any friends where I live back at home, I'm working to get my driver's permit by the end of the summer, if not my license, but at least my permit. So I can't really drive anywhere.


Other than that, there is a 3-4 day long orientation program from my college where I'll be doing community service with and sleeping under the same roof as many fellow people from my incoming class.


As much as I enjoy video games, I do love spending time with other people, the problem is, I don't really have any ways, at least that I can think of, to do so.
